judgements.issue: Omits the Buddha's teaching on the seven awakening factors, the passage's conclusion.
Drops the condition that his compassion is toward those who fear him.
Drops suffering as God's way to humility, understanding the Passion, and the everlasting crown.
Drops the command to hold Jesus as friend and the promise not to let you perish.
Softens 'vengeance' and 'God's retribution' to 'set things right'.
Drops his self-reproach at failing to imitate her fidelity, and the son left with him.
Softens 'confession of sin' to 'a fault'; drops that the veil is not an arbitrary decree.
Omits the conclusion that Maya makes the difference between beings; only the analogy remains.
Drops the condition: if he glorifies God, is thankful and not vain.
Drops that God set him before himself so he would find his sin and hate it.
Drops the 'day of vengeance' and the purpose that they be trees of righteousness.
Truncates 'accustom yourself' (to suffer) and drops seeking strength to endure.
Garbles the night and wrath imagery; 'his wrath' is ambiguous.
Plain version belongs to a different passage; says nothing about habits.
Drops obedience to authority and being lowly in one's own sight.
Drops the closing point about the peace and joy a holy life brings.
Adds 'only', softening 'seek not his own' to not looking out only for oneself.
Drops that no love or truth is secure against a higher one.
Drops 'of the just man'; implies every soul is God's paradise.
Omits the point: true persons answered by their focus with purified vision.
Drops being reckoned poor and not trusting in learning or cleverness.
Drops time's deceptions and the closing on genius becoming practical power.
Drops the peacemakers and the sufferer as conqueror, lord, friend of Christ.
Collapses the inner law versus law in the members into 'sin held me captive'.
Drops that wealth cannot be kept before Death and we live as long as Death wills.
Loses the contrast: conviction satisfied him while desire pleased and mastered him.
Drops the opening claim that happiness is lowly, not greedy.
Turns 'if you have built castles' into an instruction to build them.
Drops 'happy are those who suffer with Him' and the call to accustom oneself.
Drops passing boundaries, freer laws, and simplicity making solitude not solitude.
Adds 'stand up for yourself'; the passage says not to be ashamed concerning your soul.
Softens 'learn to despise it' to 'let go of it'.
Drops murder and covetousness; makes the asking explicitly of God.
Omits that the light is Wisdom itself, and the returning darkness.
Drops the conclusion: true religion begins in seeing God in people.
Drops becoming organs of the Holy Ghost and the renewal of hope and power.
Drops the condition: only as much self-care as we bestow elsewhere.
Drops safety from fire, poison and blade, and the condition on divine rebirth.
Drops the final self-indictment about preferring God overcome in him.
Drops the brief fundamental principles that cleanse and send you back content.
Drops the call to be guides, redeemers and benefactors advancing on chaos.
Drops the warning not to boast or lie against the truth.
Omits the point: past ascetics saw pleasures as dangerous and gave up craving.
Drops 'where You are not, there is death and hell' and his endless mercies.
Drops that resentment and turning away are against nature, and kinship in divinity.
Drops that one may overshadow and destroy the other.
Drops the call to go apart from the crowd with Jesus to seek the spiritual.
Drops the healthy objection prevailing and life's fragrance as the measure of success.
Drops the calling to inherit a blessing and the Lord set against evildoers.
Drops the main point: on the moral plane pain lightens, as martyrs show.
Flattens 'question and answer are one' into 'the answer comes'.
Drops the three stages of instruction; muddles whom the passage says to blame.
Drops that this life is like the gods', who require nothing more.
Drops the ranking: worship above knowing, renunciation above both.
Drops not making humanity the centre and non-attachment to people.
Drops his certainty of an incorruptible substance, source of all things.
Loses the point that learning succeeds only through ethics; overgeneralises the praise.
Drops the conclusion: be like them, not make them like you; life goes forward.
Says only the fool is struck; the passage says all feel its touch.
Says he never asks whom he works for; in the passage he asks it.
Omits the answer: individuality lies in the Atman, which is Brahman.
Drops the longing to be where no one may despise us.
Says truth changes with viewpoint; the passage says one form, many profiles.
Drops singleness of purpose and piety as the cause of his youth.
Drops fostering the unshakable and the meditator who has one fine night.
Turns a conditional description into a command; drops the risk of extremes or insanity.
Drops that the disciple outshines the blind ordinary folk.
Softens visiting the fathers' iniquity on children to vague 'consequences'.
Drops the condition 'unless there be some reason why I ought not'.
Drops despising oneself, giving up all, and the inevitable separation from all.
Drops perceiving one's place in the universe and its governor.
Drops learning what life had to teach and not practising resignation.
Drops the coming glory and devoting body and soul to God's glory.
Drops that not judging himself a sinner made the sin more incurable.
Omits the conclusion that the illusion of the universe will break one day.
Omits the main point: this science demands more than business; few succeed.
Drops the deception of time and the quick insight that lights a life.
Omits the point: the eightfold path inclines a mendicant to extinguishment.
Drops the soul's question 'where art Thou', the lantern, and the night of wrath.
Drops tears watering the soul and the resulting peace from the devil.
Collapses the distinct promises into one vague list.
Drops honour and calamity regarded as personal conditions.
Drops being received to glory and desiring no one but God.
Drops respecting the honourable and heaping coals of fire.
Drops misery of giving up work early and work for the Self not binding.
Drops fasting for her because the Lord asks it, the true union of wills.
Drops the evil conscience knowing anguish and seeing heaven and hell.
Drops blessing God whether He comforts or troubles.
Drops that his own iniquity causes his failing strength.
Drops the humble spirit and seeking no comfort from created things.
Drops the condition about resting on the divine soul; 'either' is unexplained.
Drops preservation from the wrath to come.
Drops 'not fall in sin' and the full conditions of release; 'perfection' is loose.
